minor.issue: Spec says 'Rejecting an already approved/rejected/completed return returns 400', but code only blocks when current status is in {rejected, completed} (not 'approved'). So an already-approved return can still be re-decided (e.g., to rejected or completed). 'approved -> completed' is actually a valid workflow transition, so this may be intentional, but the spec wording is stricter than the impl. Recommend either tightening the guard or updating the spec.

Approved-path stock restock has no idempotency guard besides the status check. If the same payload is replayed (decision=approved) against a return still in 'requested' state due to a race, stock could be incremented twice. Consider a findAndModify with status filter {status:'requested'} to atomically transition.

Refund total is computed from order item price only; it does NOT prorate discount_amount_bdt or delivery_fee_bdt. If the order had a volume discount, the refund over-refunds vs what the customer actually paid for those line items. Consider applying the order-level discount pct to each line refund.

Delivered-at detection falls back to order.created_at if no 'delivered' status_history entry exists. That means an order whose status is 'delivered' but missing history could be returnable far outside 7 days from actual delivery. Consider also storing delivered_at as a first-class field.

Customer-facing pages remain English on toggle per PRD ('incrementally translated') — flag for next iteration to expand dictionary coverage (Orders, Cart, Returns page body copy, toast messages like 'Return request submitted').

Optional: prorate order discount and/or delivery_fee when computing refund_total_bdt on POST /api/returns.
Optional: persist a first-class delivered_at timestamp on orders to avoid falling back to created_at for window checks.
Next iteration (PRD-tracked): expand i18n dictionary coverage to order/cart/returns pages and toasts.

Follow-up from iter 4 (still open): split server.py (now 2120 lines); fix <span> inside <option> hydration warning in AdminOrderDetail; return 404 on PUT/DELETE delivery-persons unknown id; make DeliveryAssignment.delivery_fee_bdt Optional[float]=None; reject negative delivery_fee_bdt; batch $in resolve in /api/service-packs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 1859 -> 2120 lines this iteration. Strongly recommend splitting into modules (auth, orders, returns, invoice, admin, packs, notifications) before next feature add.

Notification hooks are called inside try/except with broad Exception in create_order / admin_update_order_status / admin_kyc_decision / admin_assign_delivery — good defensive pattern, API unblocked on any Resend error, and when key is empty the function early-returns with a single log line. Verified log line format: '[email-skip] <to> | <subject> (RESEND_API_KEY not set)'.

Returns refund_total is computed from line price*qty only — does NOT account for order-level discount_pct/discount_amount_bdt or delivery_fee. Could over-refund on discounted orders (gold/silver tier pricing already baked into line price, but volume discount lives at order level).
PATCH /admin/returns re-decide check uses a membership test (if r['status'] in ['rejected','completed']) that leaves 'approved' re-decidable. Ambiguous against the spec wording.

Approval stock-restock is not atomic: status is read, then $inc stock, then $set status. In a concurrent re-approval this could double-increment. Use findOneAndUpdate with filter {status:'requested'} as guard.
invoice_pdf.render_invoice_pdf is called synchronously on the request path; reportlab generation is CPU-light (~3KB here) so fine for now but wrap in run_in_threadpool if volumes grow.
Float arithmetic for credit_used $inc with refund_total_bdt — same drift concern as iter 4; Decimal/paisa recommended.

rca of the issue: No defects blocking Phase 5. One spec-vs-impl ambiguity: PATCH /api/admin/returns/{id} allows re-decide on status=='approved' (code: if r['status'] in ['rejected','completed']), but the review request says rejecting an already-approved return should 400. Root cause: missing 'approved' in the disallowed-state set. Mitigation (if desired): change to `if r['status'] != 'requested'` to be strict, OR keep as-is to support the approved -> completed workflow and update the test spec. Current impl does support the approved->completed transition intentionally (common RMA workflow), so leaving as-is is defensible.
